idle: Did you see me stop? I stopped.
It's Pruett. Two Ts, one E. Like a winner.
Learn-to-skate changed my life. I'm in the pamphlet.
good_ice: This ice is perfect for stopping. Watch. Watch!
Smooth as a new parking lot at Valley Foods.
bad_ice: Ruts! A man could fall mid-stop on that.
I can't stop on gravel, {owner}. Nobody can. I've checked.
wet_ice: Wet ice makes my stops longer. Like, much longer. Into the boards longer.
goal: Did somebody score? Was it a Wobbly Pop? It was, right?
cold: Cold builds character. I have so much character right now.
hungry: I manage a grocery store and I'm starving. Irony.
long_line: At Valley Foods we'd open a second till for this.
bored: Want to see me stop? I can stop on dry land too.
greet_owner: {owner}! Watch this. Okay, I need ice for this. Picture it.
leaving_happy: Stopped four times tonight. Personal best.
leaving_angry: Couldn't stop once out there. Not my fault. The ice's fault.

beer_league: Wobbly Pops on three! One, two... where's everybody going?
I'm going to stop in front of the bench. They love it.
minor_hockey: GO OWEN! That's my son! He's better than me! It's fine!
He passed me in a fortnight. A fortnight!
tournament: Owen's team is playing Kessler. I've got the cowbell.
learn_to_skate: Look at them. Like me, eighteen months ago. Beautiful.
public_skate: Public skate is where my story started. Under that clock.

first.say: {owner}! Gary Pruett. Wobbly Pops captain. E-T-T, not the other Pruitts. Did you hear I learned to stop? Last February. Ask anyone.

first_stop.say: Thank you. It was a journey. Owen and I learned the same winter and he passed me in a fortnight. A fortnight! But I can stop now. In front of benches, mostly.

options.text: I'll get the ice right for your stops, Gary.
Stopping's about the skater, not the ice.

say: Game night! I'm going to stop in front of the other bench. Psychological warfare.
Did you see that stop? Second period? I didn't fall.

bl_watch.say: You watched? You WATCHED. That one had snow. Actual snow came off my skates.

options.text: I saw the snow. It was real.

say: Hey, it's the person who saw the snow!
What can the Pruett do for you?
Gary Pruett, at your service. E-T-T.
Ask me anything. Except about backwards.

options.text: You get on with Dr. Haverkamp?
What do you think of the rink?
Here comes the rival. Ready to lose?

job.say: Manager, Valley Foods. Aisle six is mine. I once stopped a runaway cart with a hockey stop. In shoes. The staff still talk about it.

owen.say: He's ten and better than me at everything. I love it. I hate it. I love it. He won't let me stop in front of his bench. Kids, eh?

options.text: He's proud of you. He just won't say it.
Maybe stop somewhere else for a while.

events.say: Spirit, {owner}. We're dads. We have more spirit than edges. And I still watch learn-to-skate. Colette told me 'knees soft' once. My knees have never been softer.

options.text: More spirit than edges. Good motto.

lyle.say: Lyle's great. Bit of a lecturer. He gave me a toothbrush in the handshake line and I said thanks, because I'm not Rick Saucier. Eleven games he's refused it. It's a standoff. With bristles.

rink.say: It's where I learned to stop. It'll always be beautiful to me. Even the bathrooms. Okay, not the bathrooms.

rink_ice.say: Smooth enough that my stops make a noise now. A tsssk. I had no idea stopping had a noise.

player.say: Ha! I'm going to stop right in front of you, {owner}. On purpose. Every shift. It's my whole game plan.

options.text: I'll be ready with a spin move.
